summary: Josephine County, OR state lookout: rag camp 1920, 40-ft L-4 tower 1933, 41-ft timber tower 1961; burned Nov 20, 2006 after dry rot was found.

facts.design: 41-ft treated timber tower with ODF live-in cab, built 1961, after a 40-ft L-4 tower (1933) and a rag camp (1920)
facts.status_note: Condemned and burned to the ground on November 20, 2006, after inspections found dry rot in the tower

events.note: Rag camp at the site; FFLOS describes a camp and tree platform in the 1920s
40 ft L-4 tower replaced the early platform; Weebly gives 1934 and an R-1 style cab
Staffed 120 days and reported to the Rand Ranger Station (Weebly)
41 ft treated timber tower with ODF live-in cab, built about 3/4 mile northeast of the original site
Condemned and burned to the ground November 20, 2006 after dry rot was found

corrections.why: The tower in use when the lookout burned was 41 ft (about 12.5 m), built in 1961. 12.2 m is 40 ft, the height of the earlier L-4 tower from 1933.

resolved_conflicts.field: date of the first L-4 tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites Register and the NHLR give 1933 for the L-4 tower; the Weebly summary gives 1934 and an R-1 style cab. The story uses 1933 from the registers.
FFLOS and firelookout.com say treated timber; the Weebly summary says laminated timber. The story uses treated timber.
NHLR gives 3,756 ft (1,145 m) and FFLOS gives 3,870 ft (1,180 m) for the site, with slightly different coordinates. Our brief uses NHLR's 1,144.8 m; the story reports both figures.

notes_for_editor: WebSearch was unavailable for this run (the shared search budget was spent before this tower), so nothing about the site today was checked beyond the pages read. The brief's second coordinate pair (42.60178, -123.6421, from west_us_lookouts) comes from a source not opened here. The firelookout.org index places an NHLR US 498 entry on a line next to a Clackamas County Peavine Mountain entry, while the NHLR page puts US 498 in Josephine County; worth a data check. The 1961 cab size is in the NHLR text but its quotes use curly apostrophes, so it is not recorded. The 1915-1941 details come from Weebly's quoted Forest Service station history, which was not opened directly. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the Weebly page's 2005 entry says the lookout was deemed unsafe and no longer staffed; that is compatible with 'staffed into the 2000s' and is not recorded as an event.
